sources.entry: jdsp4mac - Menu bar app that runs JamesDSP audio effects, including EQ, AutoEQ, convolver, crossfeed and ViPER-DDC, on all system audio. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Tekkiech/jdsp4mac) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that runs the JamesDSP audio effects engine (EQ, AutoEQ, convolver, crossfeed, ViPER-DDC) on all system audio using a Core Audio process tap, with no kernel extension or virtual driver.
summary.what_it_does: The app sits in the menu bar and processes everything the Mac plays through the libjamesdsp engine, using a Core Audio process tap rather than a driver. Effects include bass boost, FIR and IIR equalizers with 18 built-in presets, AutoEQ, compander, reverb, convolver with impulse responses, BS2B and HRTF crossfeed, stereo width, ViPER-DDC, vacuum tube and liveprog EEL2 scripts. Presets use the JamesDSP for Linux audio.conf format, can be imported from Linux, RootlessJamesDSP and JamesDSP for Android files, and can be tied to a specific output device. AutoEQ can search AutoEq headphone profiles or import GraphicEQ and ParametricEQ files. Selected apps can be excluded from effects. The jdspctl command-line tool controls the app and works even when the app is not running.
use_cases: apply an equalizer to all audio on a Mac
correct headphone frequency response with AutoEQ
exclude FaceTime or Safari from audio effects
script audio settings from Terminal or Shortcuts
use room or headphone impulse responses on a Mac
switch audio presets automatically per output device
how_to_run: Download jdsp4mac-<version>-arm64.zip from Releases, unzip it and move jdsp4mac.app to Applications.
Open the app, click Done on the 'Not Opened' warning, then allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
Click the menu bar icon, switch the power on and click Allow for system audio recording.
Build from source: brew install xcodegen, then run: xcodegen && xcodebuild -scheme jdsp4mac -configuration Debug build
notable: No kernel extension or virtual audio driver; audio is captured through a Core Audio process tap
Uses the JamesDSP for Linux audio.conf preset format and imports presets from Linux, RootlessJamesDSP and Android
Automatic headroom lowers output by the EQ's highest boost, up to 15 dB, to avoid limiter overload
In-app updates check that the new build is signed with the same certificate
jdspctl command-line tool shares the app's config files and works while the app is closed
caveats: Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon; the author has only tested on macOS 27.0.1 with an M1 Pro.
Stereo only: on outputs with more than two channels, only the first two channels play, and this is untested on real surround hardware.
Not notarised by Apple, so macOS requires a manual Open Anyway step on first launch; versions 0.1.2 and earlier need a manual reinstall to get in-app updates.
